q: 1. The alternatives which are stand-alone solutions for given situations in engineering involve:
options: the anticipated life of the assets
the yearly costs of maintaining the assets (annual maintenance and operation cost)
explain: A stand-alone alternative must be evaluated using its complete cost profile — first cost, useful life, and annual maintenance/operation costs — all together.

q: 2. Material cost is concerned with ......
explain: Materials that go directly into the work are a direct cost.

q: 3. A construction estimate is used
options: to judge tentatively or approximate value of the project
to produce a statement of the approximate cost
to decide an approximation of the value of the project and not the exact cost
explain: A construction estimate provides only an approximate cost of the project, not the exact final cost, which is determined only after work is completed.

q: 4. What is the element of total cost?
explain: Total cost incorporates materials, labor, energy, and equipment.

q: 5. The average cost incurred in supplying a particular benefit over the entire life time of the project is called
explain: Life cycle costing looks at the total cost of ownership over the project's lifespan.

q: 6. The types of indirect cost which can't measured and allocated to a specific output or work activity is called
explain: Overhead costs are general business expenses that cannot be attributed to a single task.

q: 7. The types of costing used to find out involved while converting a raw material to finished output, is called
explain: Process costing is used for continuous production of uniform products.

q: 8. Find the direct wage rate variance if the actual working hours are 8. If the actual and standard working rate is 15 & 12 per hour respectively.
explain: Variance = $(15 - 12) \times 8 = 3 \times 8 = 24$.

q: 9. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as ......
explain: Current assets divided by current liabilities is the current ratio.

q: 10. The benefits that is forgone by engaging the same resource in chosen activity instead of engaging the same resource in the forgone activity is known as ......
explain: Opportunity cost is the benefit given up by using a resource in one activity instead of its best alternative.

q: 11. In economic marginal cost is change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by ......
explain: Marginal cost is the change in total cost for a one-unit change in output.

q: 12. The worth of a property as shown on the accounting records is
explain: Book value is the value of an asset as recorded in the accounting/financial records, typically cost minus accumulated depreciation.

q: 13. Pick up the element of cost from the following ......
explain: Direct material, direct labour and overhead are all elements of cost.

q: 14. The wages of supervisor and material handlers are charged as ......
explain: Supervisor and material handler wages cannot be charged to a specific product, so they are charged as overhead.

q: 15. A project construction cost includes ......
explain: Construction cost covers labour and material, equipment and overhead, and the contractor's profit.

q: 16. The construction estimate of project is used by ......
explain: Owners, consultants and contractors all use the construction estimate.

q: 17. Both architect and engineer make use of the cost estimate of the project ......
explain: Cost estimates guide site selection, design and the choice between alternatives.

q: 18. Which of the following is not construction estimate?
explain: All three listed items are types of construction estimate, so 'none of these' is the item that is not an estimate.

q: 19. A review of management processes and the associated documentation is commonly called:
explain: An audit is a systematic and independent examination of books, accounts, and management processes.

q: 20. Marginal cost is:
options: The cost of producing an additional unit of a product
same to marginal revenue minus variable cost
equal to marginal revenue minus variable cost
equal to marginal revenue minus variable cost minus opportunity cost
explain: Marginal cost is defined as the additional cost incurred to produce one more unit of a product.

q: 21. Costs which are independent of output and no alteration by the change in production level are called:
explain: Fixed costs (like rent or insurance) remain constant regardless of the volume of goods or services produced.

q: 22. The sunk cost includes
options: An invested capital that can not be retrieved
explain: Sunk costs cover past expenditures, unrecovered balances, and irretrievable invested capital — all costs already incurred that cannot be recovered.

q: 23. Material cost is concerned with ......
explain: Materials used directly in the work are a direct cost.

q: 24. Directed cost of a project is due to
options: Establishment charges as salaries of administrative staff
Cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Direct cost of a project arises from costs directly attributable to production, such as the cost of materials and wages of labour.

q: 25. In economic marginal cost is the change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by
explain: Marginal cost is defined as the cost of producing 'one additional' unit.

q: 26. The additional money received from selling one more unit at a specified level of output is
explain: Marginal revenue is the incremental increase in total revenue from selling one extra unit.

q: 27. The most unpredictable cost of a project is
explain: Geological uncertainties make underground work (tunnels, foundations) notoriously difficult to estimate accurately.

q: 28. Prime cost of a project includes
explain: Prime cost is the sum of all direct costs involved in manufacturing or construction.

q: 29. Subsidy provided to private enterprises is taken as ...... for the financial analysis of any project.
explain: In financial analysis a subsidy received is treated as revenue (inflow) to the enterprise.

q: 30. The project risk that will encounter due to earthquake in which both contracting parties are unable to control the situation is ......
explain: Force majeure covers events like earthquakes beyond the control of both contracting parties.

q: 31. Supervisor's cost is ......
explain: Supervision supports many activities and cannot be charged to one item, so it is an indirect cost.

q: 32. Fixed cost can be ......
explain: A fixed cost can be direct or indirect depending on whether it can be traced to a specific item.

q: 33. Variable cost can be ......
explain: A variable cost can be direct or indirect.
